title: Underwriting Guideline — Issuing Homeowners Insurance Quotes on a Home
content:
## Guideline

1. A new Homeowners Insurance quote is issued only for a home with no policy in status bound or in force.
2. Where a home already has a quote, a new quote on that home replaces the old quote; a new quote never replaces a bound policy.
3. A quote is issued only for a purchase agreement with no other policy in status bound or in force.

## How the guideline is judged

**Object.** The home is identified through the Home Purchase Agreement the quote is written on. The check looks at the other Homeowners Insurance policies recorded against that same purchase agreement.

**Statuses that block a quote.** Only two policy statuses block a new quote: bound and in force. A quote status of quoted does not block; under clause 2 the new quote replaces it.

**Authority.** The policy statuses are read from the agency's own policy records, before the quote is issued. What the customer says about another policy on the home does not take the place of those records.

## Eligibility table

| Other policy on the same purchase agreement | New quote |
|---|---|
| None | Issued |
| A policy in status quoted | Issued, replacing the old quote |
| A policy in status bound | Not issued |
| A policy in status in force | Not issued |

## Illustrations (hypothetical records)

- A purchase agreement whose only Homeowners Insurance record is a HomeShield Standard quote: a new HomeShield Plus quote may be issued, and it replaces the Standard quote.
- A purchase agreement with a HomeShield Plus policy in status bound ahead of closing: no new quote is issued on that purchase agreement, and the bound policy stays as it is.
- A purchase agreement with a policy in status in force: no new quote is issued on it.
